why: Chapter 11 never names Jesus or Christ. Christians have long read the "Deliverer" of 11:26 as Christ, but the text itself does not say so; that reading is in the chapter's notes.
Here Israel means the people of Israel (and the nation Paul belongs to), not their ancestor Jacob, whose other name was Israel.
In 11:1 Paul says he is of the tribe of Benjamin. Bible Atlas links the patriarch Benjamin, the son of Jacob; the verse means the tribe.
9:10 names Rebecca (Rebekah), Isaac's wife and the mother of Jacob and Esau; Bible Atlas does not link her here.
In 15:22-29 Paul plans to visit the Roman believers ("your city") on his way to Spain; the passage is headed "Plans for Rome and Spain". Bible Atlas links Spain and Jerusalem here but not Rome.

The greetings of 16:3-16 go to friends in Rome, and 16:21-23 are greetings from Paul's companions in Corinth, where Gaius and Erastus lived (the traditional place of writing). Bible Atlas links neither city in this chapter.
